messages:
maria: perf-bot just flagged a regression on the canary. Qwen-7B + Mistral-draft speculative pairing shows p95 latency jump (~35%) and acceptance rate dropped to 64%. https://perf.redwood/alert/2007 :alarm_clock:
perf-bot: [ALERT] route=/generate model_pair=qwen-7b|mistral-draft p95=220ms (+35%) acceptance=0.64 (-18pp) examples=1200
jamal: ugh. did the kernel swap go out yesterday? saw the new fused attention kernels land in runtime on the same canary
alex: yes, kernel v2.3.1 rolled for all infer nodes in canary at 03:12UTC. the rollout notes said "prefer fused_attn_v2 for mixed attention shapes"
maria: can we get a quick profile? guessing it's either kernel selection falling back or KV cache being invalidated by tokenizer mismatch during the draft pairing
jamal: attaching quick flame from the canary (reduced):
```
flame: memcpy 45% | fused_attn_v2 20% | generic_mm 18% | kv_copy 10% | overhead 7%
```
jamal: looked weird — memcpy dominating. also noticed a spike in KV copy time correlated with rollout window
sophia: memcpy high often points to suboptimal memory layout or extra kv buffer churn. did the kernel change alter expected KV pack layout?
alex: kernel v2.3.1 introduced a new packed-KV path assuming RoPE scaling normalization for Mixtral-family shapes. if the pairing uses Qwen tokenizers with different stride that could cause misaligned kv lengths and trigger a slow path that copies
maria: interesting — pairing path uses speculative drafts: we keep tokenizers of primary and draft separate. if tokenizer split points differ, we do re-tokenize on the draft candidate and rebuild KV which invalidates cache and forces copy + extra decode tokens
jamal: repro script I ran:
```
# reproduce canary profile
curl -s -X POST https://canary.gen/redwood -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>", "pairing":["qwen-7b","mistral-draft"]}' | jq '.latency, .acceptance'
```
jamal: when I force the tokenizer to match (use qwen tokens for draft) acceptance recovers ~+12pp and memcpy drops 30%
sophia: so two issues colliding: (1) kernel assumes packed KV layout for Mixtral scaling -> fast path, (2) tokenizer mismatch triggers KV rebuilds and copies so we hit generic kernel fallback and lots of memcpy
alex: also saw RoPE scaling mismatch warnings in logs: `rope_scale_mismatch: scaled=1.01 expected=1.0` — might be small but it prevents the packed kernel from being used
maria: action items: reproduce minimal case, add guard to kernel selector to log why it fell back, and try temporary revert of packed-KV assumption in v2.3.1 on canary nodes
jamal: I'll add extra instrumentation: when kernel chooser picks generic_mm, log `reason=kv_layout` or `reason=rope_mismatch` and include token counts and last_kv_epoch.
sophia: for immediate mitigation we could lower speculative acceptance threshold so we avoid expensive re-tokenize fallbacks. currently acceptance_threshold=0.85 for this route. dropping to 0.78 helped in local tests but increases risk of more rerolls
alex: tradeoff: acceptance down -> more wall-clock latency (more rollouts) vs acceptance up -> more decode work per request. need metrics: p95 vs cost delta.
maria: can we do a quick AB: canary subset A with kernel revert, subset B with threshold 0.78 and added logs. run for 2 hours and compare p95 and cost/unit
jamal: scheduling that now. I'll push two variants:
- variant A: runtime kernel fallback forced false (revert packed-KV path)
- variant B: threshold=0.78 + kernel logs enabled
alex: also add a small tokenizer shim: if draft tokenizer detokenizes differently, attempt fast alignment pass that avoids full KV rebuild when delta <= 2 tokens. cheap heuristic: if token_diff <=2, patch KV tail instead of full rebuild
sophia: nice idea. cheap heuristics pay off. add opt-in via runtime flag `kv_tail_patch=true` so we can toggle without deploy rollback
maria: great. JAMAL/ ALEX/SOPHIA please add PRs and link here. we prioritize short-term mitigation (A/B) + logs so we can root cause. after that we iterate on kernel selector fix and kv_tail_patch.
jamal: PRs: https://git.redwood/pr/4201 (A/B canary), https://git.redwood/pr/4202 (kernel logs)
alex: sketch PR for kv_tail_patch in runtime: https://git.redwood/pr/4203 (WIP)
sophia: quick note: also check qwen vs mixtral head dims. some of the older kernels assume heads*kv_dim mod 64 == 0. mismatch forces copy align. check model meta on pairing list
maria: good catch. add model-metadata check to pairing validation and warn on incompatible combos
jamal: running A/B now. ETA 2h, will post intermediate perf snapshots. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: thanks. anyone see other obvious holes?
alex: just one: speculative decoder acceptance tuning interacts with batching heuristics — if we lower acceptance, we may increase batch sizes (because more samples stay in first draft), so impact on p95 might be non-linear. monitor batch distribution
sophia: i'll add batch-size histos to the logs for canary variants
jamal: snapshot 30m in: variant A p95=185ms (baseline 220ms), acceptance 0.66. variant B p95=195ms acceptance 0.76. memcpy time reduced more in A. posting full collector soon
maria: looks like kernel revert buys the most latency reduction but increases cost due to less optimized kernels on long run. we'll use revert short-term and merge kv_tail_patch + selector fix for long term
alex: agree. thanks team.
perf-bot: [RESOLUTION] incident 2007 -> mitigation applied (kernel revert on canary subset). followups: #runtime-2007 postmortem and kernel selector follow-up
maria: filing postmortem and scheduling a perf deep-dive next Tue 11:00am PT. agenda: kernel selection heuristics, kv packing invariants, tokenizer-draft alignment, speculative acceptance tradeoffs
